note: FICTIONAL Country Specifications, shaped like real ones. Regulatory lines paraphrase official sources checked on 14 Nov 2026; company details and people are invented.

items: Label IMPs under Part 7 as it stood before the 2025 amendment: regulation 46 applies Article 15 of Directive 2003/94/EC.
Each trial needs MHRA authorisation and a favourable ethics opinion before IMP is released to sites.
Label language: English (company standard).
From approved countries (initially the EU and EEA): the QP of a UK MIA(IMP) holder checks each batch's QP certification before release to the trial. The batch is not certified again.
From any other country: import and QP certification by the UK MIA(IMP) holder.
Each shipment travels with a commercial invoice and the batch's QP certification evidence.
MHRA clinical trial authorisation for each trial, tracked in the trial system.
The UK depot holds the UK MIA(IMP) used for import oversight. Licence copy filed in the quality system.
Controlled drugs need a Home Office import licence for each shipment.
No IMP in our active UK trials is a controlled drug.
Check every new IMP against the schedules of the Misuse of Drugs Regulations 2001 before its first UK shipment.
“No commercial value. Value for customs purposes only.”
“Investigational medicinal product for clinical trial use only.”
The trial reference and the UK importer of record on every invoice.

Label under Annex VI of Regulation (EU) 536/2014. The expiry date may be left off the immediate pack when the outer pack stays with it, or for blisters and small units (B.6.2 and B.6.3).

Immediate package label: “Caution: New Drug—Limited by Federal (or United States) law to investigational use.” (21 CFR 312.6(a))
No label statement may be false or misleading, or present the drug as safe or effective for what is being investigated (21 CFR 312.6(b)).
Import only under an IND in effect, for the investigation it covers (21 CFR 312.110).
Ship to investigators 30 days after FDA receives the IND, or earlier if FDA authorises it (21 CFR 312.40(c)).
Consignee: the sponsor, a qualified investigator named in the IND, or the US agent of a foreign sponsor named in the IND (21 CFR 312.110(a)).
